full_text_en:
China Everbright Bank v. Wuhan Municipal People's Government

— Dispute over Failure to Perform Statutory Duties

Ruling Summary

Although state-owned enterprises have undergone multiple restructurings and reorganizations, the debtors and guarantors and their liabilities for debts under foreign government loan projects are clear and have been confirmed by effective civil judgments, and there is no need for the people's government to re-determine the debtors and guarantors.

Administrative Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2004) Xing Zhong Zi No. 4

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): China Everbright Bank. Domicile: No. 6, Fuxingmenwai Street, Xicheng District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Wang Mingquan, Chairman of the Bank.

Agent ad litem: Yu Debin, Attorney at Beijing Jincheng Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Wuhan Municipal People's Government. Domicile: No. 130, Yanjiang Avenue, Wuhan.

Legal Representative: Li Xiansheng, Mayor of the Municipality.

Agent ad litem: Zheng Dongping, Attorney at Hubei Zheng Dongping Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wang Hui, Attorney at Hubei Zheng Dongping Law Firm.

Third Party at First Instance: Wuhan Yaguang Molding Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 9, Yingwu Xiaodao, Hanyang District, Wuhan.

Legal Representative: Li Hanqiao, Manager of the Company.

Third Party at First Instance: Wuhan Municipal Bureau of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation. Domicile: No. 298, Qingnian Avenue, Wuhan.

Legal Representative: Yang Dezhen, Director of the Bureau.

Third Party at First Instance: Wuhan Municipal Economic Commission. Domicile: No. 2, Shanhaiguan Road, Wuhan.

Legal Representative: Liu Longcheng, Director of the Commission.

Appellant China Everbright Bank, dissatisfied with the administrative judgment (2003) E Xing Chu Zi No. 1 rendered by the Hubei High People's Court in its case against Wuhan Municipal People's Government for failure to perform statutory duties, appealed to this Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel, with Adjudicator Zhao Daguang serving as the presiding judge, and Adjudicator Yang Linping and Acting Adjudicator Ma Yongxin participating in the collegial panel for the trial, with Clerk Zhao Hong keeping the record. The case is now concluded.

Facts Found by the Court at First Instance

On July 19, 1985, the Third Party at First Instance, Wuhan Yaguang Molding Co., Ltd. (formerly Wuhan No. 13 Plastics Factory, hereinafter referred to as Yaguang Company), entered into a loan contract with the Plaintiff at First Instance, China Everbright Bank (formerly China Investment Bank, Wuhan Branch, hereinafter referred to as Everbright Bank), for the introduction of a plastic turnover box project. The contract stipulated that the Plaintiff would lend to Yaguang Company USD 2,246,500 and RMB 2,269,800, with a loan term from July 1985 to March 1991. The Wuhan Second Bureau of Light Industry, the Wuhan Foreign Economic and Trade Management Committee, and the Wuhan Economic and Trade Management Committee provided guarantees for the above loan. After the contract was signed, the Plaintiff disbursed to Yaguang Company USD 1,870,100 and RMB 2,040,000 in loan proceeds.

On December 27, 1986, the Plaintiff and Yaguang Company entered into a supplementary loan contract, stipulating that the parties would increase the loan by RMB 1,000,000 based on the original loan contract, and the loan term was extended to December 1991. The Wuhan Second Bureau of Light Industry and the Wuhan Plastics Industry Company, Hubei Province, provided guarantees for this loan. After the contract was signed, the Plaintiff disbursed the above loan proceeds to Yaguang Company as agreed.

On June 8, 1990, the Plaintiff and Yaguang Company signed the "Agreement on Adjusting the Loan Contract," adjusting the loan term stipulated in the above two loan contracts to from July 1985 to October 1994. As of December 1992, Yaguang Company had repaid to the Plaintiff a total of USD 1,272,377.61 and RMB 2,189,001.31 in principal and interest.

On December 14, 1998, the Plaintiff filed a civil lawsuit with the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court, requesting that Yaguang Company and Wuhan Plastics Industry Group Co., Ltd. repay the remaining loan. On October 27, 1999, the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court rendered civil judgments (1999) Wu Min Chu Zi No. 24 and No. 26, dismissing the Plaintiff's claims on the ground that the statute of limitations had expired. The Plaintiff, dissatisfied, appealed to the Hubei High People's Court. That court, on May 29, 2000, and October 30, 2000, respectively, rendered civil judgments (2000) E Min Zhong Zi No. 43 and No. 63, affirming the above judgments of the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court.

In the meantime, Wuhan No. 13 Plastics Factory was renamed Wuhan Yaguang Plastic Products Factory on May 6, 1987. On June 19, 1990, Wuhan Yaguang Plastic Products Factory was changed to Wuhan Plastics Industry Group Company Yaguang Products Factory, with its original legal person status cancelled, and it became affiliated with Wuhan Plastics Industry Group Company. On February 22, 1994, Wuhan Yaguang Plastic Products Factory was renamed Wuhan Plastics Industry Co., Ltd. Yaguang Products Company and obtained legal person status, and on June 15, 1998, it was again renamed Wuhan Yaguang Molding Co., Ltd., which continues to this day. On March 18, 1999, the former China Investment Bank, Wuhan Branch, was taken over by Everbright Bank.

On April 17, 2002, the Plaintiff sent a letter to the Defendant, Wuhan Municipal People's Government, titled "Request Regarding the Implementation of the Repayment Responsibility of Wuhan Yaguang Molding Co., Ltd. for the World Bank On-lent Loan," requesting that, in accordance with the spirit of Guo Fa [2000] No. 15, "Notice of the State Council on Approving and Forwarding the Opinions of the Ministry of Finance and the State Development Planning Commission on Further Strengthening the Administration of Foreign Government Loans" (hereinafter referred to as Guo Fa [2000] No. 15 Document), the repayment responsibility of Yaguang Company be implemented to ensure the repayment of the World Bank on-lent loan. On September 24, 2002, the Defendant replied with letter Wu Zheng Han [2002] No. 52, stating: The debt issue between your bank and Yaguang Company was already concluded by the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court and the Hubei High People's Court in October 1999 and October 2000; regarding your bank's request that our municipal people's government implement Yaguang Company's repayment responsibility, please continue to assert your creditor's rights in accordance with the relevant provisions of national laws and regulations, and our municipality will actively cooperate in the relevant work. On December 10, 2002, the Plaintiff sent a letter to the Defendant titled "Letter Again Requesting the Wuhan Municipal Government to Re-determine the Debtor and Guarantor for the World Bank On-lent Loan Borrowed by Wuhan Yaguang Molding Co., Ltd.," to which the Defendant did not reply. On December 24, 2002, the Plaintiff filed a lawsuit with the Hubei High People's Court, requesting that the Wuhan Municipal Government perform its statutory duties.

Opinion of the Court at First Instance

The determination of an administrative organ's duties must be based on clear provisions of laws, regulations, and legally effective rules. From the legal basis cited by the Plaintiff in its lawsuit, Article 59 of the "Organic Law of the Local People's Congresses and Local People's Governments of the People's Republic of China" and the relevant provisions of Guo Fa [2000] No. 15 Document, local people's governments shall perform corresponding duties in the work of clearing overdue debts from foreign government loan projects. Although Guo Fa [2000] No. 15 Document does not explicitly state whether the clearance of overdue foreign government loans includes World Bank loans, earlier relevant documents of the State Council concerning China's sovereign external debts only used the term "foreign government loans or on-lent loans," while World Bank loans are borrowed in the name of the Chinese government. The Supreme People's Court's Fa Han [1997] No. 402 Document also clarifies that foreign government loans or on-lent loans include loans and on-lent loans from the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank. Therefore, "foreign government loans" in Guo Fa [2000] No. 15 Document shall include World Bank loans and Asian Development Bank loans, etc., as China's sovereign external debts. The Defendant's defense that the loan project involved in this case is a World Bank on-lent loan project, not a foreign government loan project, and that Guo Fa [2000] No. 15 Document is not applicable to this case, and that the document does not stipulate that local people's governments shall perform any duties regarding World Bank loan projects, cannot be sustained. However, from the provisions of Guo Fa [2000] No. 15 Document, the circumstances in which local people's governments are required to re-determine debtors and guarantors for World Bank loan projects are limited to projects that have undergone restructuring, reorganization, or bankruptcy. Although the Plaintiff's debtor, the former Wuhan No. 13 Plastics Factory, underwent multiple restructurings and reorganizations, by the time the Plaintiff filed its civil lawsuit, the debt was ultimately assumed by the Third Party in this case, Yaguang Company, and its identity as debtor was clear. The related guarantors were equally clear. Therefore, there is no need for the Defendant to re-confirm them. The reason the Plaintiff's creditor's rights could not be realized is not because its debtor and guarantors were unclear, but because when it sought to assert its creditor's rights through civil litigation, the statute of limitations had already expired. This has been confirmed by the relevant civil judgments of the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court and the Hubei High People's Court. The Plaintiff's request for the Defendant to perform statutory duties was made on April 17, 2002, and it filed the present lawsuit on December 24 of the same year. Pursuant to Article 41, Paragraph 1 of the "Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," the lawsuit was not filed beyond the statutory limitation period. The Defendant's defense that the Plaintiff's lawsuit had exceeded the statutory limitation period cannot be sustained. The Defendant's letter Wu Zheng Han [2002] No. 52 is a response to the Plaintiff's request. Although this letter did not provide a substantive response to the Plaintiff's request, it had a procedural impact on the realization of the Plaintiff's substantive rights. It constitutes a specific administrative act performed by the state administrative organ in accordance with its duties. The Plaintiff, believing that this act infringed upon its lawful rights and interests, has the right to file a lawsuit in accordance with the law. Therefore, the Defendant's request to dismiss the Plaintiff's lawsuit against this letter is not supported.

In summary, the Court at First Instance held that the Plaintiff's lawsuit had a corresponding legal basis. However, since the effective judgments of the people's court had already confirmed the civil relationship between the Plaintiff and its debtor, and the debtor and guarantor involved in the loan project had clear identities, the Defendant could not make a new determination. Therefore, the Plaintiff's claim for a judgment ordering the Defendant to perform the duty of re-determining the debtor and guarantor lacked legal basis and corresponding factual grounds and was not supported. Pursuant to Article 56, Item (1) of the "Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," the Court rendered a judgment dismissing the Plaintiff's claims; the case acceptance fee of RMB 138,295 was to be borne by Everbright Bank.

Everbright Bank, dissatisfied with the administrative judgment (2003) E Xing Chu Zi No. 1 of the Hubei High People's Court, appealed to this Court, alleging: First, the purpose of Guo Fa [2000] No. 15 Document is to solve the management mechanism for the "borrowing, use, and repayment" of loans from foreign governments and international financial organizations, and "fulfilling repayment obligations to ensure timely repayment" is its core content. To this end, the document explicitly requires that "when a project unit using foreign government loans undergoes asset restructuring, enterprise reorganization, or other changes in property rights, or bankruptcy, it must obtain prior consent from the project approval department, the Ministry of Finance, and the on-lending institution, and if necessary, also obtain the consent of the foreign party." Local people's governments at all levels "shall make corresponding adjustments and arrangements to the repayment plans for such projects, implement new debtors, and sign new on-lending agreements with the on-lending institution to ensure external repayment. It is strictly prohibited to evade debts or shirk repayment responsibilities in any form." "For projects that have already undergone restructuring, reorganization, or bankruptcy, the debtors and guarantors must be re-determined." In this case, when Wuhan Yaguang Plastic Products Factory underwent restructuring, it did not obtain the consent of the Appellant, nor did it notify the Appellant after the restructuring. This clearly constitutes an illegal restructuring and using the restructuring to evade financial debts. At the same time, according to the relevant provisions of the State Council's "Notice on Strengthening the Management of Financial Creditor's Rights During the Restructuring Process of State-owned Small and Medium Enterprises and Collective Enterprises," the Wuhan Municipal Government has the statutory duty to re-determine the debtors and guarantors. Second, the precondition for Guo Fa [2000] No. 15 Document requiring local people's governments at all levels to perform the obligation of "re-determining debtors and guarantors" is not that the subject of the debtor or guarantor does not exist, but that it requires local people's governments to "re-determine" "debtors and guarantors" with solvency to ensure the realization of the creditor's rights and thereby protect the central finance from loss. Third, the court of first instance's collection of the administrative case acceptance fee has no legal basis and should be corrected. Requested the Supreme People's Court to revoke the judgment of first instance, order the Wuhan Municipal People's Government to correctly perform its statutory duties to ensure the realization of the World Bank on-lent loan creditor's rights; the case acceptance fee should be collected according to law and borne by the Appellee, Wuhan Municipal People's Government.

Appellee Wuhan Municipal People's Government responded in its defense: The grounds of appeal of the Appellant Everbright Bank are inconsistent with the facts and misinterpret the content of Guo Fa [2000] No. 15 Document, and the judgment of first instance should be affirmed. The main reasons are: First, the entity responsible for "making corresponding adjustments and arrangements to the repayment plans for such projects, implementing new debtors, and signing new on-lending agreements with the on-lending institution to ensure external repayment" under Guo Fa [2000] No. 15 Document is the "provincial financial department or central department in the region where the project is located," not the "local government" as stated in Everbright Bank's appeal petition. Everbright Bank deliberately imposes a duty not belonging to the Respondent upon the Respondent. Second, the reason Guo Fa [2000] No. 15 Document requires the government to re-determine the debtors and guarantors of foreign government loan projects only to the extent of "projects that have already undergone restructuring, reorganization, or bankruptcy" is because the restructuring, reorganization, or bankruptcy of the loan project leads to the extinction of the legal person status of the original debtor or guarantor, making it impossible to ascertain the debtor or guarantor. However, in this case, although the subject of the loan project, Wuhan Yaguang Molding Co., Ltd., has undergone multiple name changes, its status as debtor has not changed and has been confirmed by the civil judgments (2000) E Min Zhong Zi No. 43 and (2000) E Min Zhong Zi No. 63. There is no need for the government to re-determine this. The government should not and cannot override the judiciary and make such a determination. Third, according to the provisions of Guo Fa [2000] No. 15 Document, Everbright Bank, as the on-lending bank for World Bank loans, should actively fulfill its supervisory and management duties to ensure repayment. However, the bank was negligent in managing the loan project involved in this case and did not actively assert or realize its creditor's rights, leading to its civil lawsuit being dismissed by the court on the ground of expiration of the statute of limitations. It should bear full responsibility for this. Moreover, the on-lent loan project involved in this case is a category III project; if the project unit defaults, the on-lending bank bears the responsibility of advancing external repayment. If the creditor's rights of the World Bank on-lent loan are not realized, Everbright Bank should bear the corresponding responsibility and loss itself. Requested the Supreme People's Court to dismiss Everbright Bank's appeal and affirm the judgment of first instance.

The Third Parties at First Instance, Wuhan Yaguang Molding Co., Ltd., Wuhan Municipal Bureau of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation, and Wuhan Municipal Economic Commission, did not submit defense statements to this Court.

During the first instance, the parties submitted the following main evidence to the court: the "Letter Requesting the Implementation of the Repayment Responsibility of Wuhan Yaguang Molding Co., Ltd. for the World Bank On-lent Loan" (Guang Yin Han (2002) No. 9); the "Letter of the Wuhan Municipal People's Government Regarding the Issue of Repayment Responsibility of the Debt of Wuhan Yaguang Molding Co., Ltd." (Wu Zheng Han [2002] No. 52); the "Letter Again Requesting the Wuhan Municipal Government to Re-determine the Debtor and Guarantor for the World Bank On-lent Loan Borrowed by Wuhan Yaguang Molding Co., Ltd." (Guang Yin Han (2002) No. 49); the "Notice of the State Council on Approving and Forwarding the Opinions of the Ministry of Finance and the State Development Planning Commission on Further Strengthening the Administration of Foreign Government Loans" (Guo Fa [2000] No. 15); the Chinese translation of the World Bank Loan Confirmation Letter and the "Certificate of Utilization of International Financial Organization Loans"; the "Reply of the Ministry of Finance on Confirming the List of World Bank Loan Sub-projects On-lent by China Investment Bank" (Cai Shi Bian Zi (1998) No. 114); the "Reply of the Investment Review Center of the Ministry of Finance Regarding the Use of Administrative Litigation Means to Recover After the Loss of the Case of China Everbright Bank v. Wuhan Yaguang Molding Co., Ltd." (Cai Tou Shen Han (2002) No. 172); the "Reply of the Wuhan Municipal Economic Commission on Approving the Establishment of 'Wuhan Plastics Industry Group Company'" (Wu Jing Zhuan (88) No. 355); the "Reply of the Wuhan Municipal Economic System Reform Commission on Approving the Establishment of Three Wholly-owned Subsidiaries by Wuhan Plastics Industry Co., Ltd. (Group)" (Wu Ti Gai (1993) No. 102); the Civil Judgment of the Hubei Province Wuhan Intermediate People's Court (1999) Wu Min Chu Zi No. 56; the Civil Judgment of the Hubei High People's Court (2000) E Min Zhong Zi No. 43; the Civil Judgment of the Hubei Province Wuhan Intermediate People's Court (1999) Wu Min Chu Zi No. 24; and the Civil Judgment of the Hubei High People's Court (2000) E Min Zhong Zi No. 63. The above evidence has been transferred to this Court together with the case file. After examination and verification by this Court, it can be used as the basis for ascertaining the facts of this case. The facts found by this Court based on the above evidence are identical to those in the original judgment.

Opinion of the Court

According to the provisions of State Council Document Guo Fa [2000] No. 15, which stipulates that "local people's governments and relevant central departments shall be responsible for clearing up the debts of projects utilizing foreign government loans in their respective regions and departments; all relending banks shall actively and promptly provide relevant data. The responsibilities for repayment and guarantee of repayment shall be further clarified and implemented. For projects that have undergone restructuring, reorganization, or bankruptcy, the debtor and guarantor must be re-determined," the World Bank on-lending loan involved in this case falls within the category of foreign government loan projects. This is further corroborated by the Ministry of Finance's Cai Wai Zi No. 685 (1982) document titled "Report on Submitting for Approval the World Bank's Loans to China's Intermediary Financial Institutions" and the Ministry of Finance's Cai Shi Bian Zi No. 114 (1998) document titled "Reply on Confirming the List of Sub-Projects Under the World Bank On-Lending Loans of China Investment Bank." The Wuhan Economic Commission's Wu Jing Zhuan (88) No. 355 document and the Wuhan Economic System Reform Commission's Wu Ti Gai (1993) No. 102 document indicate that Wuhan Yaguang Molding Co., Ltd. is a project that has "undergone restructuring or reorganization" as defined in Guo Fa [2000] No. 15. Therefore, the appellee, the Wuhan Municipal People's Government, has the statutory duty to determine the debtor and guarantor for the on-lending loan project that has been restructured or reorganized.

Guo Fa [2000] No. 15 provides that for projects that have undergone restructuring, reorganization, or bankruptcy, the local people's government shall re-determine the debtor and guarantor. This is to clarify and implement the responsibilities for loan repayment and guarantee. If the debtor and guarantor are clear, there is no need to re-determine them. In this case, although the debtor, the former Wuhan No. 13 Plastic Factory, has undergone multiple restructurings and reorganizations, the identities and responsibilities of the debtor and guarantor are clear and have been confirmed by an effective civil judgment. Therefore, there is no need for the people's government to re-determine the debtor and guarantor. The appellant, China Everbright Bank, argues that the prerequisite for Guo Fa [2000] No. 15 requiring local people's governments at all levels to fulfill the obligation of "re-determining the debtor and guarantor" is not that the debtor and guarantor entities do not exist, but rather that the local people's government is required to "re-determine" a "debtor and guarantor" with the ability to repay. This ground of appeal lacks legal basis. The reason the appellant's creditor's rights in this case cannot be realized is that the statute of limitations for asserting such rights has expired. Regarding the classification of foreign government loan projects into three categories under Guo Fa [2000] No. 15, this provision applies to loan projects after 2000 and does not make classifications for on-lending loan projects prior to that date. The appellee, the Wuhan Municipal People's Government, argued in its defense that the on-lending loan project involved in this case falls under the third category and that the project entity should bear the repayment responsibility. This argument cannot stand.

The dispute in this case is whether the Wuhan Municipal People's Government should fulfill its duty to re-determine the debtor and guarantor for the on-lending loan project, and it does not directly involve the amount of property. The court of first instance's collection of a case acceptance fee of RMB 138,295 was improper and should be corrected.

In conclusion, the appellant's claim requesting a judgment ordering the Wuhan Municipal People's Government to fulfill its duty to confirm the debtor and guarantor of the on-lending loan in this case lacks corresponding legal and factual basis. The judgment of the first instance found the facts clearly and applied the laws and regulations correctly. Pursuant to Article 61(1) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

The case acceptance fees for the first instance and the appeal are RMB 100 each, to be borne by the appellant, China Everbright Bank.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Zhao Daguang

Judge: Yang Linping

Acting Judge: Ma Yongxin

June 7, 2004

Court Clerk: Zhao Hong
